newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end softer on high margin loans.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end softer on high margin loans.

text.p: Taiwan share prices opened higher but ended slightly lower on Friday as caution emerged over a record-high level of margin loans outstanding, brokers said.
The index lost 14.19 points or 0.21 percent to end at 6,587.44. Turnover was an active T$47.87 billion.
"The record-high T$236.2 billion in margin loans outstanding announced on Thursday shows investor confidence, which is good," said National Securities investment manager Allen Huang.
"But the index is at a comparatively high level compared with the stagnant domestic economy, which so far has not shown any apparent recovery," he said.
The index opened higher following Thursday's modest rise but failed to test resistance at 6,650 points, brokers said.
"Seeing the index fail to break 6,650 resistance, cautious investors turned to take profits first," Huang said.
Brokers said the central bank's pledge on Thursday to maintain a stable-to-loose monetary policy had been discounted.

"But the central bank board meeting passed a reserve requirement reform proposal that will gradually lower banks' reserve requirements, which is good news in the long run," said Michael Hung, head of research at Nikko Securities.
Constructions fell most, with BES Engineering down 40 cents to T$27.6. Recently bullish electronics saw profit-taking, with United Microelectronics down 80 cents to T$37.4.
Automotive, electrics, steel and machinery shares rose slightly. Copper shares surged on rising international copper prices, with S&T Copper up T$1.1 to T$26.5.
Brokers said they expected further profit-taking pressure in coming sessions. For Saturday, a 6,500-6,600 range was seen.
